belongs_to: Figure it Out Q1: 'The dot plots below show the distribution of the number of pockets on clothing for a group of boys and for a group of girls' - the left plot, titled Boys
description: Left one of two side-by-side dot plots printed for comparison. Title 'Boys' above the plot. Horizontal number axis with tick labels 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 (7 at the right end) and axis title 'Number of Pockets' (italic) below it. No vertical axis, no vertical numbers. Background is a light grid: a vertical gridline at every integer 0-7 (the one at 0 is a darker left axis line) and horizontal gridlines one dot-height apart (room for 6 stacked markers). Markers are orange filled triangles, one per boy, stacked upwards from the baseline on the integer they belong to. Counted stacks: 0 -> none, 1 -> none, 2 -> none, 3 -> 1 triangle, 4 -> 4 triangles, 5 -> 5 triangles, 6 -> 2 triangles, 7 -> none. Total 12 triangles (1+4+5+2). Tallest stack is at 5 (5 high); the data run from minimum 3 to maximum 6.

belongs_to: Figure it Out Q8 'Standing tall in the storm.' (a) estimate the number of skyscrapers in New York, Tokyo and London; (b) validity of statements about Mumbai and Hong Kong
description: Horizontal bar graph (an infographic) on a dark brown background. White title 'Cities with Most Skyscrapers' with the smaller white subtitle '(buildings taller than 150m)'. 20 horizontal gold bars, one per city, all starting at the same left baseline, listed top to bottom in decreasing length. Left of each bar: the city name (right-aligned, white) and a small national-flag icon between the name and the bar. Each bar has its value printed in white just beyond its right end, except three bars whose value is deliberately left blank. There is NO axis line, NO tick marks, NO gridlines and NO scale. Rows in order (city: value): Hong Kong 553; Shenzhen 367; New York (no value printed); Dubai 251; Guangzhou 188; Shanghai 183; Tokyo (no value printed); Kuala Lumpur 154; Chongqing 144; Jakarta 112; Bangkok 110; Singapore 95; Mumbai 86; Seoul 82; Toronto 81; Melbourne 69; Miami 58; Istanbul 48; Moscow 46; London (no value printed). So 17 values are printed and 3 are hidden (New York, Tokyo, London). The bars are drawn roughly to scale: measured on the page picture, the Hong Kong bar is the longest and the hidden bars are about 57% (New York), 30% (Tokyo) and 5% (London) of its length, which is what students use to estimate. In the lower right corner, behind the bottom rows, a grey photo-style skyline of famous skyscrapers (about 20 towers, e.g. a pair of tall twin towers, a spired tower, the Hong Kong glass tower) is drawn as decoration only. Counting from the list: 12 cities are above Mumbai (Hong Kong ... Singapore) and 7 cities are below it (Seoul ... London).
unclear: The three hidden values (New York, Tokyo, London) are not printed anywhere in the book; the percentages above come from measuring the bars in the page image and are estimates only.
Bar lengths are only approximately proportional to the printed values: Mumbai (86) is drawn as long as Seoul (82), and Jakarta (112) as long as Bangkok (110).

Flag icons are small; flags are assumed to be: Hong Kong, China (Shenzhen, Guangzhou, Shanghai, Chongqing), USA (New York, Miami), UAE, Japan, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore, India, South Korea, Canada, Australia, Turkey, Russia, UK.
